rationale: A wins because it keeps the story honest under pressure: “which leg of the transfer the stablecoin actually replaces” is exactly the question a payments reporter will ask before wasting a minute. B is competent, but it starts spending facts it does not have with “cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story”; that may be true, but right now it is a spreadsheet-shaped wish. A has one overcooked phrase in “skipping correspondent banks,” but it immediately interrogates that claim instead of building a fourth angle on it.
gaps_in_A: “skipping correspondent banks” overstates the release; the facts say faster and cheaper than correspondent banking, not that Wise has fully bypassed banks.
“the trend a market's edge case becomes its plumbing” is a little magazine-y and needs outside evidence; A correctly asks for it, but the headline still leans ahead of the proof.
“where the regulators say yes” is strong, but without actual launch markets it remains a reporting assignment, not yet a pitchable story.
gaps_in_B: “One of the biggest cross-border payment networks” is not directly supplied; £30B per quarter supports scale, not a global ranking claim.
“remittance company” muddies the B2B payment update and pulls the story toward consumer money transfer.
“cutting correspondent-banking fees is a margin story” assumes Wise's own unit economics improve; the update only says businesses can move money faster and cheaper.
The counterposition angle asks for a SWIFT or bank comment but misses the more basic proof: which stablecoin, which partner, and which settlement leg is actually replaced.
